correctness.rationale: Nielsen's cited finite input was checked in the original for odd p including composites and exactly the inclusive all-ties threshold. The new phase-coordinate polynomial has disjoint ±1 slices, so realification commutes with every threshold without taking the real part at the original frequencies. Orthogonality of the second phase harmonic gives the exact squared-projection average, hence positive measure independent of the source amplitude. In the block argument a witnessing threshold can be replaced by the smallest coefficient magnitude actually selected, so it selects no later block and all earlier ones. Norm bounds and arbitrarily large input amplitude are compatible because each scalar is fixed before choosing the next finite model. Block events are independent; finite amplification yields the zero-mean large-measure witness, and summable infinitely many blocks plus Borel–Cantelli prove spectral avoidance. Verified the real-space Baire step: a regular positive threshold has a uniform gap from all coefficient magnitudes by Bessel finiteness above half that threshold. The finite selected sums then vary uniformly, and strict superlevel measure persists by approximation from above in the level. Conversely a.e. unboundedness gives the finite-threshold witness to every open set condition via countability, even after discarding thresholds at least 1/k (only finitely many sums). Hence the divergence set itself is dense G-delta. Every full magnitude level is the same initial segment for all allowed enumerations, giving one common full-measure set.
residual_risks: Frozen numerical checker does not prove the finite large-amplitude input or the infinite claim and was not run. Conclusions apply to real functions on odd cyclic products, not to every infinite compact abelian group.

value.rationale: Real Fourier data have conjugate ties, and density in the complex space does not settle the problem for real functions. The phase-coordinate identity gives an exact real construction compatible with the nonlinear threshold operation, and its finite high-measure outcome is strong enough for generic divergence and finite-spectrum avoidance on every odd base. This fills the real-valued gap rather than restating the established all-orderings corollary.
residual_risks: No quantitative optimal block dimension or general real compact-group theorem is claimed.
